title: What is a cache?
subtitle: A bookshelf beats a long walk.
takeaway: A cache keeps useful copies nearby. Freshness still matters.

boards.heading: The long way
boards.note: Fetch it from the original source.

boards.heading: Keep a copy nearby
boards.note: Check nearby before making the trip.

boards.heading: Fast is not always fresh
boards.note: Copies can become out of date.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Pip, why does this page load faster the second time?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: It remembered something useful. That is caching.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Give me the version without computer words.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Imagine walking to the library every time you need the same book.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Even if I only forgot one sentence?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Exactly. So you keep a copy on your desk. The next lookup is much quicker.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: The desk copy is the cache?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Yes. An app can keep a nearby copy instead of fetching the same thing again.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Then why not keep that copy forever?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: The original might change. A quick answer can still be an old answer.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: So check the age, or replace it when something changes.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Right. Fast access, with a plan for keeping copies fresh.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: My desk has a caching system. It is called a very large pile.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Your next lesson is cache eviction.
